summary.name: ImHex
summary.one_liner: ImHex is a free, open source hex editor for reverse engineers and developers, with a Pattern Language, data analysis, visualization and disassembly tools.
use_cases: Describing and validating binary file formats
Disassembling x86, ARM and other machine code
Analyzing entropy and byte patterns in raw data
Automating tests of generated binary files in CI/CD
summary.what_it_does: ImHex lets users open binary data and decode it into a tree structure using its Pattern Language, with colored field segmentation and the ability to modify individual field values. It includes analysis and visualization tools such as entropy and byte type graphs, a data inspector that decodes data in over 40 formats, and 3D model, sound and image visualizers. A built-in disassembler supports over 25 instruction sets including x86, ARM and Intel 8051, with Intel and AT&T syntax options and the ability to decode bytecode from live processes. It also offers a command line interface and plugin support for integrating into CI/CD workflows.
notable: Pattern Language for describing binary formats as a tree, with support for over 300 existing file formats
Built-in disassembler for over 25 instruction sets with custom disassembler support
Command line interface and plugins for CI/CD testing of generated files
caveats: Listed on awesome-mac as freeware and the project is open source on GitHub; the page does not state any paid tiers
